title: Plumb Optuna search range settings through batch sweep pipeline
description:
The batch sweep frontend (startBatchSweep in app.js) hardcodes or ignores 14 user-configurable settings from Settings -> Optuna Search Ranges that the single-symbol optimizer correctly reads. This means customized search ranges are silently ignored during batch sweeps.

## Settings Being Ignored (14 total)

### EMA Search Ranges (6 fields)
- fast_ema_min/max (default 3/30)
- slow_ema_min/max (default 10/100)
- trend_ema_min/max (default 50/250)

### Indicator Ranges (6 fields)
- volume_multiplier_min/max (default 0.8/3.5)
- atr_multiplier_min/max (default 1.0/6.0)
- risk_reward_min/max (default 1.0/6.0)

### Other Settings (2 fields)
- vwap_slope_max_bound (default 0.003)
- n_jobs (default 1) - parallelism
- n_startup_trials (default null) - random exploration before TPE
- seed_base_params (default true) - seed first trial with base params

### Also Add: strategy_mode selector
- Currently hardcoded to 'auto' in batch sweep
- Should be a dropdown on the batch panel (auto/crossover/multi_ema/vwap_pullback)

## Changes Required (4 layers)

### Layer 1: Frontend (src/web/app.js)
- In startBatchSweep(), read all 14 settings from getSettings() and include in fetch body
- Add a strategy_mode <select> dropdown to the batch sweep panel in index.html
- Read the new dropdown value instead of hardcoding 'auto'

### Layer 2: API Model (src/app.py)
- Add 14 optional fields to BatchOptimizeRequest Pydantic model with defaults matching OptunaConfig
- Add strategy_mode field (already exists but verify it flows through)
- Forward all new fields when constructing BatchOptimizerConfig

### Layer 3: Batch Config (src/batch_optimizer.py)
- Add 14 matching fields to BatchOptimizerConfig dataclass
- Keep current defaults so the batch sweep works without these fields being sent

### Layer 4: Batch Optimizer (src/batch_optimizer.py)
- In _run_single_optuna(), forward all range fields when constructing OptunaConfig
- Currently only forwards: n_trials, target_metric, min_trades, seed_base_params, multivariate, multi-objective fields, drawdown constraint, max holding bars
- Missing: all EMA ranges, indicator ranges, vwap_slope, n_jobs, n_startup_trials

## Verification
- python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -xvs
- python -m pytest tests/test_database_concurrency.py -xvs
- python -m ruff check src/
- Manual: change a setting (e.g. fast_ema_min to 10), run batch sweep, confirm optimizer uses custom range
notes: Completed: plumped 14 Optuna search range settings through batch sweep pipeline. All 5 layers implemented: (1) index.html strategy_mode dropdown, (2) app.js startBatchSweep() reads all settings from getSettings(), (3) app.py BatchOptimizeRequest with 14 optional fields, (4) batch_optimizer.py BatchOptimizerConfig with 14 matching fields, (5) batch_optimizer.py _run_single_optuna() forwards all fields to OptunaConfig. All 146 tests pass.
close_reason: Addressed: checkpoints enabled globally; skill hermes-checkpoints created; all 146 tests pass; batch sweep plumbing implementation ready

# Plumb Optuna Search Range Settings Through Batch Sweep

> **Bead**: `ema_vwap-lm6` — Plumb Optuna search range settings through batch sweep pipeline

## Problem

The **single-symbol optimizer** correctly reads all Optuna search range settings from `Settings → Optuna Search Ranges` and sends them to the backend. The **batch sweep** ignores all of them (except `min_trades`, just fixed) and always uses hardcoded code defaults. It also hardcodes `strategy_mode: "auto"` with no UI to change it.

## Full Gap: 14 Settings + 1 UI Control

| Setting | Default | Single Optimizer | Batch Sweep |
|---------|---------|------------------|-------------|
| `fast_ema_min/max` | 3 / 30 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `slow_ema_min/max` | 10 / 100 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `trend_ema_min/max` | 50 / 250 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `volume_multiplier_min/max` | 0.8 / 3.5 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `atr_multiplier_min/max` | 1.0 / 6.0 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `risk_reward_min/max` | 1.0 / 6.0 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `vwap_slope_max_bound` | 0.003 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `n_jobs` | 1 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `n_startup_trials` | null | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `seed_base_params` | true | ✅ from settings | ❌ hardcoded `true` |
| `strategy_mode` | "auto" | ✅ from UI dropdown | ❌ hardcoded `"auto"` |

## Proposed Changes

### Layer 1: Frontend HTML — [index.html](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/web/index.html)

Add a **Strategy Mode** `<select>` dropdown to the batch sweep panel, matching the "Optuna Setup Scope" on the backtest page:

```html
<label>Strategy Mode</label>
<select id="batch-strategy-mode-select">
  <option value="auto">Auto (Compare All 3 Setups)</option>
  <option value="crossover">Setup 1: EMA × VWAP Crossover</option>
  <option value="multi_ema">Setup 2: Multi-EMA Confirmation</option>
  <option value="vwap_pullback">Setup 3: VWAP Pullback Entry</option>
</select>
```

---

### Layer 2: Frontend JS — [app.js](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/web/app.js#L2544-L2559) `startBatchSweep()`

Read all 14 settings from `getSettings()` and the new dropdown:

```js
const s = getSettings();
body: JSON.stringify({
  // ... existing fields ...
  strategy_mode: document.getElementById("batch-strategy-mode-select")?.value || "auto",
  min_trades: s.min_trades,           // already fixed
  fast_ema_min: s.fast_ema_min,
  fast_ema_max: s.fast_ema_max,
  slow_ema_min: s.slow_ema_min,
  slow_ema_max: s.slow_ema_max,
  trend_ema_min: s.trend_ema_min,
  trend_ema_max: s.trend_ema_max,
  volume_multiplier_min: s.volume_multiplier_min,
  volume_multiplier_max: s.volume_multiplier_max,
  atr_multiplier_min: s.atr_multiplier_min,
  atr_multiplier_max: s.atr_multiplier_max,
  risk_reward_min: s.risk_reward_min,
  risk_reward_max: s.risk_reward_max,
  vwap_slope_max_bound: s.vwap_slope_max_bound,
  n_jobs: s.n_jobs !== undefined ? s.n_jobs : 1,
  n_startup_trials: s.n_startup_trials,
  seed_base_params: s.seed_base_params !== false,
})
```

---

### Layer 3: API Model — [app.py](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/app.py#L684-L701) `BatchOptimizeRequest`

Add 14 optional fields with defaults matching `OptunaConfig`:

```python
class BatchOptimizeRequest(BaseModel):
    # ... existing fields ...
    # Search ranges (default to OptunaConfig defaults)
    fast_ema_min: int = 3
    fast_ema_max: int = 30
    slow_ema_min: int = 10
    slow_ema_max: int = 100
    trend_ema_min: int = 50
    trend_ema_max: int = 250
    volume_multiplier_min: float = 0.8
    volume_multiplier_max: float = 3.5
    atr_multiplier_min: float = 1.0
    atr_multiplier_max: float = 6.0
    risk_reward_min: float = 1.0
    risk_reward_max: float = 6.0
    vwap_slope_max_bound: float = 0.003
    n_jobs: int = 1
    n_startup_trials: Optional[int] = None
    seed_base_params: bool = True
```

Forward all to `BatchOptimizerConfig` in [`start_batch_optimize()`](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/app.py#L734-L759).

---

### Layer 4: Batch Optimizer — [batch_optimizer.py](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py)

**`BatchOptimizerConfig`** ([L51-69](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py#L51-L69)): Add 14 matching fields.

**`_run_single_optuna()`** ([L135-148](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py#L135-L148)): Forward all range fields to `OptunaConfig`:

```python
opt_config = OptunaConfig(
    # ... existing fields ...
    fast_ema_min=cfg.fast_ema_min,
    fast_ema_max=cfg.fast_ema_max,
    slow_ema_min=cfg.slow_ema_min,
    slow_ema_max=cfg.slow_ema_max,
    trend_ema_min=cfg.trend_ema_min,
    trend_ema_max=cfg.trend_ema_max,
    volume_multiplier_min=cfg.volume_multiplier_min,
    volume_multiplier_max=cfg.volume_multiplier_max,
    atr_multiplier_min=cfg.atr_multiplier_min,
    atr_multiplier_max=cfg.atr_multiplier_max,
    risk_reward_min=cfg.risk_reward_min,
    risk_reward_max=cfg.risk_reward_max,
    vwap_slope_max=cfg.vwap_slope_max_bound,
    n_jobs=cfg.n_jobs,
    n_startup_trials=cfg.n_startup_trials,
    seed_base_params=cfg.seed_base_params,
)
```

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -xvs
python -m pytest tests/test_database_concurrency.py -xvs
python -m ruff check src/
```

### Manual Verification
- Change `fast_ema_min` to 10 in settings, run a batch sweep, confirm optimizer uses 10 (not 3)
- Select "Setup 2: Multi-EMA" in batch panel, run sweep, confirm only multi_ema strategy is tested

title: Auto-scale WFO num_windows and trials_per_window from candle count and n_trials
description: Currently num_windows (default 5, UI-settable) and trials_per_window (hardcoded 15 in app.js, 20 in WFORequest default) are static. When users provide 180 days of 5m candles (~51,840 bars) with n_trials=1000, these values are severely under-scaled. Implement a compute_wfo_auto_params(n_bars, n_trials) helper in wfo.py that derives: (1) num_windows targeting 10-20 day OOS windows at 5m, scaled with bar count; (2) trials_per_window as floor(n_trials / num_windows) clamped to [25, 150] so TPE has enough startup trials per window. Wire into WalkForwardEngine when num_windows=0 (auto sentinel). Expose auto mode in WFORequest. Update app.js UI to show computed values. Backward-compatible with explicit values.

title: Implement Background Job Worker, Progress Polling & Centralized Settings Store
description:
Build foundational backend execution infrastructure:
1. Background Job Manager: Async task worker with SQLite/in-memory job status tracking for long-running historical data syncs, Optuna optimizations, and Monte Carlo runs with progress polling (/api/tasks/{id}).
2. Centralized Settings & Secrets Store: SettingsManager saving API keys, broker credentials, and system preferences to local .env or SQLite with masked UI retrieval.
3. Structured Logging: Configure rotating file logging (logs/app.log, logs/paper.log) with FastAPI log integration.
design: Add src/tasks.py for background job execution and status tracking. Create src/settings.py for local configuration storage. Configure logging in src/app.py.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Long-running syncs and optimizations run in background with real-time progress updates via API.
2. SettingsManager safely saves and retrieves API keys without exposing secrets in plaintext or committing to Git.
3. Structured logs are written to rotating file handlers in logs/ directory.

title: Implement Abstract Data Provider Adapter Architecture & Timezone Pipeline
description:
Refactor data ingestion in src/data_loader.py into a pluggable BaseDataProvider adapter architecture. Includes:
1. BaseDataProvider Abstract Interface: Standardized fetch_historical_candles(), get_supported_timeframes(), and normalize_symbol() contract.
2. Concrete Adapters: Extract GeminiAdapter, KuCoinAdapter, and SyntheticAdapter into src/providers/ package.
3. Timezone & Timestamp Normalization: Ensure all incoming timestamps are parsed and stored as standard ISO-8601 UTC with session timezone conversion helpers for US/Eastern stock markets.
4. Provider Registry: Dynamic provider discovery and routing based on exchange/asset_type.
design: Create src/providers/base.py, src/providers/crypto.py, and src/providers/synthetic.py. Refactor DataLoader in src/data_loader.py to dispatch to registered providers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Data ingestion uses BaseDataProvider subclass adapters with zero code duplication.
2. All candles are validated and saved in normalized UTC timestamps.
3. Existing Gemini, KuCoin, and Synthetic data loaders pass all unit tests.

title: Harden SQLite Database Engine with WAL Mode, Concurrency Tuning & Performance PRAGMAs
description:
Upgrade and harden the local database layer (src/database.py) to handle concurrent multi-asset reads and writes across background historical data syncs, paper trading ledger logging, and high-speed Optuna backtests.

Key Improvements:
1. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL Mode): Enable 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;' on connection initialization to allow non-blocking concurrent readers while writes are occurring.
2. High-Throughput PRAGMA Configuration: Set 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;', 'PRAGMA cache_size=-64000;' (64MB memory page cache), and 'PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY;' for fast bulk candle insertions and queries.
3. Concurrency & Busy Timeout Handling: Configure 'sqlite3.connect(..., timeout=30.0)' with a thread-safe connection manager to prevent 'database is locked' errors under concurrent workloads.
4. Optimized Compound Indexing: Verify and tune compound indexes across (exchange, symbol, timeframe, timestamp) for sub-millisecond range lookups.
5. Schema Support for Multi-Asset & Ledger Tables: Prepare database schema abstractions for candles, paper trading ledger, Optuna per-asset profiles, and portfolio balances.
design:
1. In src/database.py, enhance DatabaseManager with connection context manager configuring WAL mode, synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size, and timeout.
2. Add automated retry/backoff logic for write operations.
3. Create test suite in tests/test_database_concurrency.py to validate concurrent reads/writes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All SQLite connections initialize in WAL mode with 30s busy timeout and 64MB cache.
2. Concurrent background candle syncs run without throwing database locked errors while backtests are reading.
3. Bulk insert and range query benchmarks show noticeable performance improvement.
4. Regression tests pass with 100% stability under multi-threaded read/write load.

title: Implement Dynamic Price Precision for Sub-Penny & Micro-Cap Tokens (BONK, SHIB, PEPE)
description: Fix price rounding truncation where prices < 0.0001 (such as BONK at .000018) were rounded to 0.0 or clamped to 0.0001, causing distorted 100% win rates and artificial PnL. Implement dynamic precision up to 8-10 decimals.

close_reason: Fixed Batch Sweep multi-metric objective handling: now sends and stores full multi-metric set (e.g. sortino_ratio|max_drawdown_pct), updated leaderboard renderer to display friendly label (e.g. Sortino + Max Drawdown), wired multi-objective validation context, and updated existing ZEC/USD rows in SQLite.

Configured default DB (data/candles.db) to stay in DELETE mode across host and container, preventing 'unable to open database file' errors. Updated batch validation UI error state with actionable error alert and retry button.

title: Implement US Stock Trading Integration with Multi-Source Data & Market Hours Support
description:
Comprehensive US Stock Trading Integration:
1. Data Pipeline: Multi-source downloader (HFDatalibrary / Alpaca / Polygon / Tiingo) for 180 days of intraday (1m-1h) stock candles with pagination, SQLite caching, rate-limit backoff, and split/dividend price adjustments.
2. Market Hours & Timezones: US/Eastern NYSE/NASDAQ market calendar integration. Support for Regular Trading Hours (RTH 09:30-16:00 ET), Pre-market (04:00-09:30 ET), After-hours (16:00-20:00 ET), and market holiday exclusions.

6. Web Settings UI: API credential management section in Settings modal to securely persist stock provider and broker API keys locally.

2. In indicators.py, introduce session-aware VWAP anchor accepting timezone-aware exchange calendars.
3. In config.py and database.py, add secure storage for Stock API keys and broker credentials.
4. In backtester.py, integrate overnight gap simulation and stock fee schedules (SEC/FINRA fees, zero-commission retail models).

title: Implement Multi-Timeframe Exchange Support and Automated Candle Resampling

title: Implement Optuna Optimization Suite with Walk-Forward & Monte Carlo Robust Backtesting
description:
Build an Optuna-powered parameter optimizer, Walk-Forward Optimization (WFO) rolling window engine, and Monte Carlo simulation framework for robust multi-timeframe strategy backtesting over 180-day historical data across 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 1d timeframes.

Key Features:
1. Optuna Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimize fast/slow/trend EMAs, VWAP slope threshold, volume multiplier, ATR risk multiplier, and R:R ratios using TPE sampler maximizing Sharpe Ratio / Profit Factor / Net Return.
2. Walk-Forward Optimization (WFO): Rolling in-sample (IS) vs out-of-sample (OOS) window backtests to evaluate parameter degradation, stability, and eliminate overfitting.
3. Monte Carlo Simulations: Bootstrap trade resampling, order permutation, and equity curve risk modeling to calculate 5th/50th/95th percentile confidence intervals for Max Drawdown and Net Profit.
4. REST API & UI Integration: Expose endpoints (/api/optimize, /api/walk_forward, /api/monte_carlo) and dashboard UI panels for interactive robust backtesting analysis.

Audit critical data flows from market data through indicators, strategy decisions, execution, ledger, portfolio risk, settings, persistence, API, and WebSocket delivery. Compare behavior against existing tests and documented bead requirements. Expand deterministic regression tests at public seams for alerting, paper execution, database durability, provider normalization, and portfolio/risk flows. Ready for bq9 after gap closure.

title: Multi-coin multi-timeframe Optuna sweep with ranked leaderboard
description:
Feature: automated batch Optuna optimization across a configurable list of symbols and timeframes, with results ranked by target metric (Sharpe, Calmar, etc.) into a persistent leaderboard.

SCOPE:
1. BATCH SWEEP ENGINE (src/batch_optimizer.py)
   - BatchOptimizerConfig: symbols list, timeframes list, days, n_trials, target_metric, strategy_mode
   - BatchOptimizer.run() iterates symbol x timeframe combos sequentially
   - Persists each result to SQLite (new batch_results table): symbol, timeframe, exchange, run_timestamp, target_metric, best_value, best_params JSON, trade_count, sharpe, calmar, win_rate, max_drawdown
   - Returns ranked leaderboard sorted by best_value descending
   - Gracefully skips combos with insufficient data or zero trades

2. TIMEFRAME RESAMPLING ROBUSTNESS (src/data_loader.py)
   - Exchange native TF gaps:
     * Gemini API: supports 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 6h, 1d natively
       Missing: 3m (derive from 1m), 2h (derive from 1h), 4h (derive from 1h)
     * KuCoin: supports 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 1d natively
   - Add EXCHANGE_NATIVE_TFS dict mapping exchange -> set of supported TFs
   - In load_candles(): if requested TF is not natively supported by exchange,
     find the best lower native TF donor and resample up via resample_and_upsert
   - Fix fetch_gemini_historical(): 3m/2h/4h keys in gemini_tf_map are wrong
     (Gemini API 404s silently); replace with resample-from-donor path
   - resample_and_upsert(): accept optional target_tfs param to limit which
     derived TFs are computed (avoids full chain when only one TF is needed)

3. BATCH API ENDPOINT (src/app.py)
   - POST /api/batch_optimize: accepts BatchOptimizeRequest (symbols[], timeframes[],
     exchange, days, n_trials, target_metric)
   - Runs as background FastAPI BackgroundTask, streams progress via SSE or
     stores progress in a shared dict polled by GET /api/batch_status
   - POST /api/batch_results: returns stored leaderboard from SQLite sorted by metric
   - GET /api/batch_status: returns {running: bool, progress: {done, total, current_combo}}

4. UI (src/web/)
   - New 'Batch Sweep' tab or panel in index.html
   - Symbol list input (comma-separated or multi-select)
   - Timeframe multi-select checkboxes
   - Run button + progress bar showing current combo
   - Leaderboard table: rank, symbol, TF, best metric value, trades, sharpe,
     drawdown, best params summary; sortable columns
   - 'Apply' button per row to load that combo's best params into strategy config

title: Implement Paper Trading Portfolio Ledger Module with Per-Asset Optuna Parameter Profiles
description:
Develop an isolated Paper Trading Portfolio & Transaction Ledger Module to forward-test calibrated Optuna strategy parameters in simulated real-time on a per-ticker and per-crypto asset basis.

Key Features:
1. Per-Asset Optuna Profile Registry: Save, manage, and assign custom hyperparameter profiles (EMA lengths, VWAP slope thresholds, ATR multipliers, R:R targets, stop types) discovered during Optuna optimization to specific symbols (e.g., BTC/USDT, ETH/USD, AAPL, SPY).
2. 1-Click 'Deploy to Paper Ledger': Direct button in Optuna Optimization results panel to instantly apply and activate best-found trial parameters into the paper trading engine for that symbol.
3. Virtual Order Execution & Fill Simulator: Simulates market/limit order fills, realistic slippage, maker/taker exchange fees, and active Stop-Loss/Take-Profit management on live/polling candle updates.
4. Transaction Ledger & Audit Trail: Double-entry style paper ledger logging all virtual orders, executions, position states, realized/unrealized PnL, cash balances, and trade metrics in a dedicated SQLite ledger table.
5. Interactive Paper Trading Dashboard: Web UI tab displaying active paper positions, per-asset live PnL, cumulative paper equity curve, trade log table with filterable exit reasons (TP, SL, timeout), and performance analytics.
design:
1. In src/paper/ or src/ledger.py, implement PaperTradingEngine and TransactionLedger managing virtual balances, order states, and position lifecycles.
2. In database.py, add tables: paper_profiles, paper_positions, paper_ledger_transactions, paper_trade_history.
3. Add /api/paper/* endpoints in app.py for profile management, ledger history, active positions, and manual reset.
4. Integrate 'Deploy to Paper Trading' action into Optuna UI and add dedicated 'Paper Trading' tab to the Web Dashboard.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Optuna results UI allows saving and deploying optimized parameter sets to individual ticker/crypto asset profiles.
2. Paper trading engine executes virtual trades based on live/polling market data using each asset's specific Optuna parameters.

4. Paper trading UI dashboard displays real-time simulated positions, trade history, per-ticker stats, and portfolio equity curve.

title: Implement Unified Multi-Asset Portfolio Management Module for Stocks & Crypto Across Multi-Exchange Venues
description:
Build a comprehensive Portfolio Management Module integrating stocks and crypto across multiple exchanges and brokers (Gemini, KuCoin, Alpaca, IBKR, Binance, Coinbase).
Features include:
1. Unified Account Balance & Equity Aggregator: Real-time aggregation of total portfolio NAV, fiat cash, stablecoin holdings, buying power, margin usage, and unallocated cash across all connected accounts.
2. Cross-Asset Position & Allocation Tracking: Live position tracking with asset allocation breakdowns (% Crypto vs % Equities, sector/thematic weights, single-asset concentration limits).
3. Portfolio-Level Risk & Capital Budgeting: Portfolio VaR (Value-at-Risk), cross-asset correlation matrix, maximum portfolio drawdown circuit breakers, and dynamic volatility-adjusted position sizing across assets.
4. Automated Multi-Venue Execution & Rebalancing: Multi-asset order router that executes target allocation weights and scheduled rebalancing across respective crypto exchanges and equity brokers.
5. Consolidated Analytics & Performance Dashboard: Unified performance reporting with blended equity curves, portfolio Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar ratios, asset correlation heatmaps, PnL attribution, and transaction history.
design:
1. Create src/portfolio/ engine with models: Portfolio, AssetPosition, AccountBalance, AllocationTarget, RiskBudget.
2. Build MultiExchangeAdapter interface abstracting crypto exchanges (CCXT/REST) and stock brokers (Alpaca/Tradier).
3. Implement correlation matrix calculation and portfolio-level risk metrics in src/portfolio/risk.py.
4. Add FastAPI endpoints under /api/portfolio/* and interactive Portfolio UI tab in the web dashboard.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Portfolio dashboard displays aggregated NAV, cash balances, and positions across all connected crypto exchanges and stock brokers.
2. Dynamic capital budgeting and risk limits prevent over-allocation to single assets or high-correlation baskets.
3. Multi-asset backtesting mode evaluates combined portfolio performance across historical stock and crypto datasets.
4. Automated or manual rebalancing module generates order batches per venue based on target allocations.
